info.title: OpenVibe.Bot API
info.description: Routes of OpenVibe.Bot as the OpenVibe contracts describe them (openvibe-contracts 0.245.0): each operation lists the capabilities it performs; a token for the service's audience must carry one of them unless the route is open. Generated by openvibe-contracts lib/openapi.js; do not edit.

post.summary: Manage robots with a Network service token: create one for the person the body's owner or X-OV-Subject names (a new robot and its pairing code), and, for any robot id, rename, reconfigure or delete it
post.description: **bot.robot.manage** (first-party): Manage robots with a Network service token: create one for the person the body's owner or X-OV-Subject names (a new robot and its pairing code), and, for any robot id, rename, reconfigure or delete it (irreversible), issue a one-time pairing code, add or remove operators, clear its e-stop, and rotate a paired device's credentials (the new credential and publish key are shown once) or revoke the device, which closes its socket at once. Bot does not check the acting person against the robot's owner for a service token (a person's own token must be the owner's).

post.description: **bot.job.dispatch** (internal): OpenVibe.Run hands a platform.job@1 to a paired Node over the device link and reads its state: POST /api/v1/jobs {node_id, job, project_id, subject, provider} dispatches it (idempotent by job id; 409 bot.class_unadvertised when the device does not advertise the job's class), POST /api/v1/jobs/:id/cancel cancels it, GET /api/v1/jobs/:id returns its state with the captured stdout. project_id is required (422 without it): the dispatch carries the project, and Run is the payer. parameters.name: ttl_ms

schema.description: Lifetime from the worker's receipt of the job, covering any wait and the run; the worker caps it with its own local maximum (the stricter wins, as with `max_command_ms`). When it runs out, a job not yet started never starts and a running one is killed; either way `job_exit` says `ttl`.

When it runs out, a job not yet started never starts and a running one is killed; either way `job_exit` says `ttl`.

parameters.name: limits

schema.description: Caps the worker enforces on the running process (merged stricter with its local caps); exceeding one kills the job and `job_exit` says `limit`.

parameters.description: Caps the worker enforces on the running process (merged stricter with its local caps); exceeding one kills the job and `job_exit` says `limit`.

parameters.name: net

schema.description: Network policy; absent means `deny`. `none` is `deny` spelled as OpenVibe.Node's worker.egress names it; `public` and `openvibe-only` ask for egress the host must already allow (ADR-046): a worker whose host policy is stricter runs the stricter one, and a worker that cannot enforce what is asked refuses the job (`nack`) rather than running it weaker.

parameters.name: inputs

schema.description: Files placed in the job's working directory before the process starts. Each is an OpenVibe.Media object pinned by digest: a size or digest mismatch ends the job failed before the process ever runs (run.job.input_digest_mismatch). Never a caller-chosen URL and never a credential; the worker holds its own token. Names are unique and carry no path separator.

post.summary: OpenVibe.Run's sessions on machines (the Desks plan's D6): lease one desk for one session and act on it, with a Run service token naming the session's person in X-OV-Subject.
post.description: **bot.desk.session** (first-party): OpenVibe.Run's sessions on machines (the Desks plan's D6): lease one desk for one session and act on it, with a Run service token naming the session's person in X-OV-Subject. POST /api/v1/machines/:id/desk-leases (bot.desk-lease-create-request@1, answered by bot.desk-lease@1) starts a browser desk on the person's own machine where they let agents use it, or on a desk host whose owner offers its desks to other people and whose Node sandboxes every desk; POST /api/v1/machines/:id/desk-leases/:desk/commands carries screen, input and browser (bot.command@1 without desk) to that desk alone; DELETE /api/v1/machines/:id/desk-leases/:desk stops it. Bot takes it only from Run, never reaches another desk or the machine itself, and on a shared host keeps even its owner off a leased desk.

post.summary: Control a person's robots through the authority's control API (ADR-048 amendment 2026-10-15, step 8 phase 2): POST /api/v1/resources/control takes one common.owned-resource-control-request@1 naming a
post.description: **bot.resource.control** (first-party): Control a person's robots through the authority's control API (ADR-048 amendment 2026-10-15, step 8 phase 2): POST /api/v1/resources/control takes one common.owned-resource-control-request@1 naming a bot.robot (id rob_<ULID>) from a first-party service (OpenVibe.Services) acting for the person in on_behalf_of. Actions: stop (latch the robot's remote e-stop, as POST /api/v1/robots/:id/estop: every actuator stops and nothing moves until it is cleared) and resume (clear that e-stop, as POST /api/v1/robots/:id/estop/clear; a local stop on the robot itself still holds); any other action is refused unsupported. Only the resource's owner may act: the request's owner must be the owner the authority holds. dry_run decides and explains without applying. The first answer per (caller, idempotency_key) is kept and returned for a repeat; the same key with another request is refused. Answers common.resource-control-result@1 without resource (person-owned resources have no OVRN).

get.summary: Read robots with a Network service token.
get.description: **bot.robot.read** (first-party): Read robots with a Network service token. GET /robots needs ?owner= and lists that person's robots; the robot routes answer for any robot id with role "service": Bot does not check X-OV-Subject or any person's membership for a service token (a person's own token is held to owner, operator or viewer). Devices never carry a credential or key hash. The command audit (GET /robots/:id/audit, newest first, paged) is read too, for any robot id. Bot also requires this capability, beside bot.robot.control, to latch the e-stop.

post.summary: Physically control a robot with a Network service token.
post.description: **bot.robot.control** (first-party): Physically control a robot with a Network service token. POST /robots/:id/estop latches the e-stop for any robot id and needs bot.robot.read as well; Bot records the service as the actor and does not check X-OV-Subject. On the operator WebSocket (/control) a token with this capability must name a person in X-OV-Subject, and Bot applies that person's role (owner, operator or queue), allowlist and limits. Clearing the e-stop is bot.robot.manage. The operator WebSocket frames are bot.command@1, answered by bot.command-result@1; a refused command is audited and emits bot.command.refused.

bot.desk-lease-create-request.v1.title: BotDeskLeaseCreateRequest
bot.desk-lease-create-request.v1.description: bot.desk-lease-create-request@1 (the Desks plan's D6): the body of POST /api/v1/machines/{id}/desk-leases on OpenVibe.Bot (capability bot.desk.session), answered 201 with bot.desk-lease@1. DESK is the name Run chose for the session (unique per session); a desk already leased to another session, or running for the machine's owner, is refused 409 bot.desk_busy, and a repeat for the same session answers its lease (200). A machine with no room (its max_desks) is refused 409 bot.machine_busy, one that is offline 409 bot.device_offline, and one the person may not use 404 bot.device_not_found.

bot.desk-lease.v1.title: BotDeskLease
bot.desk-lease.v1.description: bot.desk-lease@1 (the Desks plan's D6): one desk OpenVibe.Bot holds for one OpenVibe.Run session, as POST /api/v1/machines/{id}/desk-leases answers it (201, capability bot.desk.session, a Run service token acting for the session's person in X-OV-Subject) and GET /api/v1/machines/{id}/desk-leases/{desk} reads it. The request is bot.desk-lease-create-request@1. Bot leases a desk only on the person's own machine where they turned on 'Let my agent use this computer' (shared false), or on a desk host whose owner offers its desks to other people and whose OpenVibe.Node runs each desk in its own sandbox (describe desk.isolation sandbox; shared true). The lease starts the desk (bot.command@1 kind desk, start, kind browser, the lease's size) and from then on only the lease's person, through Run, may act on that desk, with screen, input and browser at POST /api/v1/machines/{id}/desk-leases/{desk}/commands (bot.command@1 without desk, answered by bot.command-result@1): never another desk, never the machine's own screen, files, programs or network, and on a shared host not even its owner's own commands reach a leased desk. DELETE /api/v1/machines/{id}/desk-leases/{desk} stops the desk and ends the lease; so does the machine going away (Run sees the lease gone, 404, and ends the session host_lost).

owner.description: The session's person, the only one whose commands reach the desk.

shared.description: true on a desk host that serves other people (the desk runs in its own sandbox there); false on the person's own machine.

bot.device-connect-result.v1.title: BotDeviceConnectResult
bot.device-connect-result.v1.description: bot.device-connect-result@1: answers of OpenVibe.Bot's device credential routes, which Bot gates with bot.robot.manage (bot.device.connect is reserved, not enforced). POST /api/v1/devices/:id/rotate → { device, credential, publish_key } (both secrets shown once); POST …/devices/:id/revoke → { device } (its socket closes at once).

bot.device.v1.title: BotDevice
bot.device.v1.description: bot.device@1: a paired device as the API presents it (domain.present.device): never a credential or publish-key hash; online is added when a robot's devices are listed.

bot.job-dispatch-result.v1.title: BotJobDispatchResult
bot.job-dispatch-result.v1.description: bot.job-dispatch-result@1: what OpenVibe.Bot answers OpenVibe.Run's bot.job.dispatch calls (server/api/v1.js and server/jobs/index.js). POST /api/v1/jobs is 201 { job, sent }: `job` is Bot's run_jobs record and `sent` says whether the `job` frame went out on the device link now (false while the paired Node is away; it is resent on every reconnect until the Node acks it). POST /api/v1/jobs/:id/cancel is 200 { job, sent } with the same shape: `sent` says whether a `job_cancel` frame went out. GET /api/v1/jobs/:id is 200 { job, stdout }: the record plus the last 1 MiB of the job's captured stdout, or null when the Node sent none. The record's `state` follows the run_jobs lifecycle queued -> placed (the Node acked) -> running (job_started) -> one end state, and its `job` field is the platform.job@1 body Run dispatched, stored and resent verbatim. A refused dispatch answers a problem instead (422 bot.invalid_job, 404 bot.device_not_found, 409 bot.class_unadvertised, 409 bot.job_id_reused), never this contract.

job.description: One run_jobs row as presentJob renders it: what Run dispatched, to which device, and how far the job and its metering have come.

id.description: The platform.job@1 id Run minted and the stem of every usage reading key (run:<id>:<n>).

node_id.description: The paired device the job was sent to; a Node never reads another device's job.

state.description: queued (stored; sent and resent until acked), placed (the Node acked it), running (job_started), then one end state from job_exit: succeeded (exited 0), failed (another exit code, or reason limit, stopped or failed, or a nack), cancelled (a cancel before start, or reason cancelled), expired (reason ttl).

project_id.description: The payer project Run named; required on every dispatch (422 without it).

subject.description: The subject the readings are for (user:usr_…), as Run sent it; null when Run sent none.

provider.description: The offer's provider, as Run sent it; null for a first-party node.

cancel_requested.description: A cancel was asked for this job; a job not yet started is cancelled at once, a running one ends with its job_exit.

fault_code.description: The Node's nack fault code, or why Bot stopped sending the job (bot.class_unadvertised); null while it is still sendable.

sent_at.description: First time the `job` frame went out (epoch ms); null while queued and never sent.

started_ms.description: The Node's job_started started_ms: the anchor of every usage second; null until it started.

finished_at.description: When the first job_exit settled the job (epoch ms); null until then, and for a job cancelled before it started that no job_exit ever settled.

exit_reason.description: The first job_exit's reason (platform.job-frame@1); null until it arrived.

exit_code.description: The process's exit status; null when it was killed or never ran.

wall_ms.description: job_exit.usage.wall_ms as billed, capped at the job's limits.wall_ms; null until job_exit.

usage_read.description: Wall-clock seconds of the job already queued for Billing; only moves forward.

result.description: The job_exit result (any JSON); null unless a job_exit carried one.

job.description: The platform.job@1 body Run dispatched, stored and resent verbatim; present on every stored job.

created_at.description: Epoch ms Bot first stored the job.

updated_at.description: Epoch ms of the last change to the row.

stdout.description: The last 1 MiB of a job's captured stdout, held in memory by Bot (job_stdout chunks; a chunk_seq already held is dropped, and older chunks fall off once the ring is full).

text.description: The held chunks joined in order.

first_seq.description: The chunk_seq of the first held chunk; null when none is held.

last_seq.description: The highest chunk_seq seen for the job; 0 when none.

truncated.description: True when an earlier chunk fell off the 1 MiB ring.

dispatched.description: The answer of POST /api/v1/jobs (201) and POST /api/v1/jobs/:id/cancel (200): the row and whether the frame went out on the link now.

sent.description: True when the `job` (dispatch) or `job_cancel` (cancel) frame was written to the device's link; false when the device is away (a job is resent on reconnect until acked).

state.description: The answer of GET /api/v1/jobs/:id (200): the row and the job's held stdout (null when the Node sent none).

bot.robot-control-result.v1.title: BotRobotControlResult
bot.robot-control-result.v1.description: bot.robot-control-result@1: answers of bot.robot.control on OpenVibe.Bot. POST /api/v1/robots/:id/estop → { robot } with its e-stop as it now stands.

bot.robot-manage-request.v1.title: BotRobotManageRequest
bot.robot-manage-request.v1.description: bot.robot-manage-request@1: bodies of bot.robot.manage on OpenVibe.Bot. POST /api/v1/robots → { owner (the person a service acts for), name, profile_id, access_policy?, limits? }; PATCH …/robots/:id → { name?, access_policy?, limits? }; POST …/robots/:id/operators → { subject, role? (operator by default) }. POST …/robots/:id/pairing-code and both DELETE routes take no body.

bot.robot-manage-result.v1.title: BotRobotManageResult
bot.robot-manage-result.v1.description: bot.robot-manage-result@1: answers of bot.robot.manage on OpenVibe.Bot. POST /api/v1/robots → 201 { robot, pairing }; PATCH …/robots/:id and POST …/robots/:id/estop/clear → { robot }; DELETE …/robots/:id → 204 (no body); POST …/robots/:id/pairing-code → 201 { code, expires_at, installer }; POST …/robots/:id/operators → 201 { operators }; DELETE …/robots/:id/operators/:subject → { operators }; POST …/devices/:id/rotate and /revoke → bot.device-connect-result@1.

pairing.description: A one-time pairing code (shown once), when it expires and the one-line installer command that uses it.

anyOf.description: A one-time pairing code (shown once), when it expires and the one-line installer command that uses it.

bot.robot-read-request.v1.title: BotRobotReadRequest
bot.robot-read-request.v1.description: bot.robot-read-request@1: the query of bot.robot.read on OpenVibe.Bot (server/api/v1.js); the routes take no body. owner names whose robots GET /api/v1/robots lists (a service must give it; a person may give only their own subject). limit (1 to 200, default 50) and before (the last audit id seen) page GET …/robots/:id/audit.

bot.robot-read-result.v1.title: BotRobotReadResult
bot.robot-read-result.v1.description: bot.robot-read-result@1: answers of bot.robot.read on OpenVibe.Bot (a service token needs no acting subject: only GET …/robots needs ?owner=). GET /api/v1/robots?owner= → { robots }; GET …/robots/:id → { robot, role }; GET …/robots/:id/operators → { operators }; GET …/robots/:id/devices → { devices } (no hashes, with online); GET …/robots/:id/audit?limit=&before= → { audit, next_before } (newest first).

bot.robot.v1.title: BotRobot
bot.robot.v1.description: bot.robot@1: a robot on OpenVibe.Bot as its API presents it (domain.present.robot): its owner-chosen name, the device profile it runs, who may drive it (access_policy) and the latched e-stop.

common.owned-resource-control-request.v1.title: OwnedResourceControlRequest
common.owned-resource-control-request.v1.description: common.owned-resource-control-request@1 (ADR-048 amendment 2026-10-15, step 8 phase 2): one control operation on a person-owned resource. Robots, chat rooms, restream definitions and pastes belong to a person, not to a project, so they carry no OVRN and the project-scoped common.resource-control-request@1 cannot name them. OpenVibe.Services sends this to the owning authority's POST /api/v1/resources/control (the same route, told apart by `owned`), acting for the person in on_behalf_of. owned names the resource by its index summary's kind and id. owner is the person it belongs to: the authority refuses unless its own record says the same (Services also offers actions only on the viewer's own resources). A sensitive action (deleting, physical control) asked by an agent is refused with confirmation_required until the owner approves, as for project resources. idempotency_key makes a retry safe: the authority answers a repeated key from the same caller with the first result, and refuses the key reused with another request. Answered with common.resource-control-result@1 (without resource: there is no OVRN). The actions each authority takes are in its <service>.resource.control capability; any other action is refused unsupported.

owned.description: The resource, as its owning authority's resource index lists it (common.resource-summary@1 kind and id).

id.description: The summary's id: a prefixed ULID (rob_…) or the service's own slug (a paste, a room).

owner.description: The person the resource belongs to. Person-owned resources belong to people, never to agents or apps.

params.description: Action-specific input, shaped by the authority's own contract (never redefined here).

on_behalf_of.description: Who asks: the owner, or their agent (whose sensitive actions wait for the owner's approval).

confirmation_id.description: The approved confirmation from an earlier confirmation_required answer.

common.resource-control-result.v1.title: ResourceControlResult
common.resource-control-result.v1.description: common.resource-control-result@1: the authority's answer to a common.resource-control-request@1 (ADR-048, plan T13). state is the outcome, not the resource's own state: done (applied), pending (accepted and asynchronous; the authority reports completion later on its events), refused (a policy or confirmation gate said no) or failed (an error). State rules: refused carries problem or confirmation_required; failed carries problem; done and pending carry neither; confirmation_required appears only on refused. result carries the authority's own response document and never another service's rows. The state rules are checked by contracts.resources.checkControlResult.

confirmation_required.description: The action needs its owner's approval; retry the same request with this confirmation_id once approved.

problem.description: RFC 9457 body when refused or failed.

common.resource-list-result.v1.title: ResourceListResult
common.resource-list-result.v1.description: A page of the resource index (roadmap WS-Z7).

partial.description: Authorities a merged index (OpenVibe.Services, ADR-048) could not read for this page: a slow or failing authority is omitted, never fails the page. Each entry names the authority and the problem code it answered. Added in 1.1.0; a single authority's own index leaves it out.

common.resource-name.v1.title: ResourceName
common.resource-name.v1.description: common.resource-name@1: the one stable, cross-service name of an OpenVibe resource (OVRN; ADR-034 section 2, ADR-048, plan T13): ovrn:<service>:<project_id>:<type>/<id>, for example ovrn:media:prj_01J0000000000000000000000A:object/med_01K0000000000000000000000B. The service segment is the authority that owns the resource; the project segment is its tenancy boundary; type is the second half of a common.resource-summary@1 kind and id is that summary's id, so the name composes from any resource summary. It is used in grant scopes, audit rows, event subjects, usage records, bill lines and console URLs. It never names a person, an app, a request, a session or an event. The pattern is the one common.usage-recorded@1 resource and common.resource-summary@1 ovrn already use.

common.resource-summary.v1.title: ResourceSummary
common.resource-summary.v1.description: One resource of any service, as the resource index lists it (roadmap WS-Z7): every service answers GET /api/v1/resources with these, so OpenVibe.Services shows any resource without owning its data.

kind.description: service.kind, e.g. watch.watch, actor.actor, media.object, events.subscription

ovrn.description: Optional resource name (ADR-034 section 2), the name grants, audit, events, usage records and bills use: ovrn:<service>:<project_id>:<type>/<id>, e.g. ovrn:watch:<project_id>:watch/<wch_id>, with the pattern of common.usage-recorded@1 resource. Its service, project and id are this summary's service, project_id and id. Added in 1.1.0.

errors.problem.v1.title: Problem
errors.problem.v1.description: RFC 9457 problem details (application/problem+json) with a stable OpenVibe error code and trace identifiers. The legacy 'error' string is allowed during migration so existing clients keep working.

error.description: Deprecated compatibility field: same text as title/detail for clients that read {error}.

identity.subject-ref.v1.title: SubjectRef
identity.subject-ref.v1.description: The one cross-platform reference to an actor. Issued by OpenVibe.Network. Never a service-local integer id.

oneOf.description: AgentSubject: an agent (OpenVibe.Actor, or a developer app's agent) acting under grants its owner delegated (roadmap WS-Z2). In an event envelope, on_behalf_of names the owner.

platform.job.v1.title: Job
platform.job.v1.description: platform.job@1: one unit of work a dispatcher (OpenVibe.Bot now, Fabric later) hands to an execution worker (plan T14 Run; ADR-034 proposed). It rides the device control link inside a `job` frame (platform.job-frame@1). The worker answers it with `ack` (accepted) or `nack` (refused: an unknown or unimplemented class, a missing artifact, limits it cannot honor, the local kill switch), then runs it at most once. Metering: a running `function` job is billed by wall-clock second as platform.usage-sample@1 readings; platform.job-frame@1 `job_usage` gives the mapping.
platform.job.v1.$comment: Additive optional fields may extend this v1 contract.

id.description: Minted by the dispatcher (job_<ULID>): the idempotency and ack key, as a Node command `id` is. A worker that already holds or ran this id never runs it again: a resent `job` is acked again while it runs and answered with its `job_exit` once it ended. Never reused: it is the stem of every usage reading's key (`run:<id>:<second>`).

artifact.description: The pre-registered artifact to run; required for classes `function` and `code`.

version.description: One exact version, never a range

args.description: The artifact's declared input as JSON; the whole `job` frame stays within the link's 1 MiB frame limit.

ttl_ms.description: Lifetime from the worker's receipt of the job, covering any wait and the run; the worker caps it with its own local maximum (the stricter wins, as with `max_command_ms`). When it runs out, a job not yet started never starts and a running one is killed; either way `job_exit` says `ttl`.

limits.description: Caps the worker enforces on the running process (merged stricter with its local caps); exceeding one kills the job and `job_exit` says `limit`.

net.description: Network policy; absent means `deny`. `none` is `deny` spelled as OpenVibe.Node's worker.egress names it; `public` and `openvibe-only` ask for egress the host must already allow (ADR-046): a worker whose host policy is stricter runs the stricter one, and a worker that cannot enforce what is asked refuses the job (`nack`) rather than running it weaker.

inputs.description: Files placed in the job's working directory before the process starts. Each is an OpenVibe.Media object pinned by digest: a size or digest mismatch ends the job failed before the process ever runs (run.job.input_digest_mismatch). Never a caller-chosen URL and never a credential; the worker holds its own token. Names are unique and carry no path separator.

platform.runtime-class.v1.title: RuntimeClass
platform.runtime-class.v1.description: platform.runtime-class@1: the kind of execution environment a platform.job@1 asks for (plan T14 Run; ADR-034 proposed). A name only: this contract defines no behavior, and a worker runs only the classes it advertises and refuses every other one (`nack`). `function` is the first class implemented (OpenVibe.Node's function worker); the others are reserved names. Each class names one reserved Fabric capability in platform.resource-offer@1.capabilities — `worker:` + the class (worker:function, worker:code, worker:browser, worker:linux, worker:desktop, worker:gpu) — and a node advertises the name of each class it runs.
platform.runtime-class.v1.$comment: Additive: a class may be added to v1; none is removed, renamed or reordered.

oneOf.description: A pre-registered artifact (name and exact version) run once with declared args to one result: single-shot, no persistent filesystem, no dependency resolution, network denied.
Arbitrary source with its dependency tree in a longer-lived environment; needs image handling and isolation stronger than a container.
A headless or headed web browser session driven remotely.
A full Linux environment (shell, filesystem, processes) that lives across commands.
A graphical desktop session with screen and input under control levels.
A workload that holds one or more GPUs for its lifetime.

run.session.v1.title: RunSession
run.session.v1.description: run.session@1 (the Desks plan's D6): one session on OpenVibe.Run, a browser desk held for one person, as GET /api/v1/sessions/{id} answers it (capability run.session.read) and run.session-list-result@1, POST /api/v1/sessions (run.session.create) and POST /api/v1/sessions/{id}/end (run.session.control) carry it. A session is a desk (bot.command@1 kind desk, kind browser) that Run places on a machine and OpenVibe.Bot leases to it (bot.desk-lease@1): on one of the person's own machines where they let agents use it (trust user-owned, never another person's), or on a desk host that serves other people (trust first-party or community: the host's OpenVibe.Node runs every desk in its own sandbox, desk_isolation sandbox, and offers nothing else of the machine). STATES: placing (stored, looking for a machine) -> starting (the desk is leased and starting) -> running (the desk answered) -> ended. An ended session never changes; end.reason says why: ended (POST /api/v1/sessions/{id}/end), ttl (ttl_s ran out), idle (no command for idle_s), host_lost (its machine went away or stopped the desk), unplaceable (no machine had room before ttl_s, or none at all) or failed (the desk would not start). USAGE: desk_seconds counts from started_at to ended_at (or now while running), metered to OpenVibe.Billing as one platform.usage-sample@1 per minute (service run, operation browser.desk, unit s, idempotency_key run:<session id>:<minute>). Run mints the id (ses_<ULID>).

owner.description: The person the session is for: only they (or a first-party service acting for them) read, act on or end it.

via.description: The first-party service that asked for the person (service:actor), or null when they asked themselves.

kind.description: A platform.runtime-class@1 name; browser (a headless browser driven over its pipe) is the only kind of session in v1.

ttl_s.description: The most the session lives, from created_at.

idle_s.description: A session no command used this long ends (end.reason idle).

size.description: The desk's page size (bot.command@1 kind desk width and height).

machine.description: The machine (OpenVibe.Bot device) the desk runs on.

desk.description: The desk's name there (bot.command@1 desk), leased to this session alone.

trust.description: The offer's trust class (platform.resource-offer@1): user-owned is always the owner's own machine.

offer_id.description: The platform.resource-offer@1 it was placed on; null when the request named the person's own machine.

reasons.description: Why this machine, in a few words each (the placer's reasons).

started_at.description: When the desk first answered (state running).

desk_seconds.description: Seconds the desk ran (started_at to ended_at, or to now while running); 0 when it never started.

reasons: a shared desk host with room

openvibeToken.description: An OpenVibe Network token for this service: a person's token, an app token (client credentials, audience of the service) or a first-party service token. Its `cap` claim must include the capability the operation names.

x-openvibe-other-bindings.binding: POST /api/v1/machines/:id/commands with kind exec, fs or screen (bot.command@1, answered by bot.command-result@1 with data)
POST /api/v1/machines/:id/commands with kind ai (bot.command@1, answered by bot.command-result@1 with data)
WS /control {type:"command"} (bot.command@1, answered by a command_result frame, bot.command-result@1)
